correctness.rationale: For a \(C^2\) convex boundary, total signed curvature is \(2\pi\) and curvature is nonnegative, so a point with positive curvature \(\kappa\) exists. In tangent coordinates, \(f(\pm t)=\kappa t^2/2+o(t^2)\) and \(f'(\pm t)=\pm\kappa t+o(t)\). The two V-edges through \(X_t=(0,\kappa t^2)\) have slopes \(\pm\kappa t/2+o(t)\), hence the unique reflex turn has magnitude \(\kappa t+o(t)\). The simple dented curve therefore has total absolute curvature \(2\pi+2\kappa t+o(t)\). The removed arc has length \(2t+\kappa^2t^3/3+o(t^3)\), whereas the two V-edges have total length \(2t+\kappa^2t^3/4+o(t^3)\), so the perimeter perturbation is cubic. Thus the average curvature is \(2\pi/p+(2\kappa/p)t+o(t)\). The removed cap has thickness \(O(t^2)\). If \(B(o,r)\subset\operatorname{int}K\), the homothetic contraction with \(\varepsilon=Mt^2\) has inward clearance at least \(Mrt^2\); for fixed sufficiently large \(M\), it lies inside the dented cell and has average curvature \(2\pi/((1-Mt^2)p)=2\pi/p+O(t^2)\). The positive linear term then forces strict violation for all sufficiently small \(t\). The unit-circle computation was only a consistency check.

originality.rationale: Larson's full primary text explicitly identifies failure for arbitrarily small dents of smooth convex curves as an expected corollary of a conjectural smooth extension and says that this corollary should be approachable, but does not prove it. The new claim proves an existential version for every \(C^2\) convex curve by a local V-dent and homothetic competitor. Exact-form, alias, and implication searches found no later indexed result covering this theorem. The main residual risk is an unindexed note or treatment under different terminology.

value.rationale: Larson explicitly isolates failure for arbitrarily small dents of smooth convex curves as a natural missing corollary of his polygonal theory. The theorem resolves that boundary phenomenon for every \(C^2\) convex curve and identifies the mechanism quantitatively: geometric dent depth and the cost of an interior homothetic competitor are \(O(t^2)\), while the reflex turn raises the cell's average absolute curvature by a positive \(O(t)\) term. This is a motivated structural result about stability of a classical convex-geometric inequality, not a routine specialization, isolated numerical value, or recomputation.
